If I could change the world in one way, I would make sure every person has guaranteed, secure access to the fundamentals of a dignified life: reliable food and clean water, basic healthcare, safe shelter, and high‑quality education that teaches both skills and critical thinking.

Removing those basic scarcities would immediately reduce preventable suffering and death, and over time it would lower crime and conflict, unlock human potential and creativity, and create more stable, prosperous societies better able to address longer‑term problems like climate change. It’s not a utopia by itself, but it rearranges incentives and opportunities in ways that make most other improvements—from governance to innovation—far easier and more equitable.
